# The Roving Office

> A soft-3D isometric office that shows what your coding agents are doing, live. Each agent session becomes a character who walks in, sits down, does the work you asked for and leaves — watchable in a browser, shareable by link.

The office runs locally or on a URL, takes live events from several
coding-agent harnesses over a small HTTP protocol, and needs no account: an office is
addressed by an unguessable eight-character keycard, which is the whole of its access
control for reading.

The two documentation sets below are strictly separated and it is worth honouring. *For
everyone* assumes a browser and nothing else. *For developers* assumes a checkout and an
intent to change something.

## For agents

If you are an AI coding agent and somebody has asked you to connect **this session** to
the office, do not assemble it from the pages below. There is one document written for
you, it is authoritative, and it is meant to be fetched and followed:

- [Set up The Roving Office](https://therovingoffice.com/agent-setup/prompt.md): mint an office, install the adapter for your own harness, restart the session.

What it will ask of you, so you know before you fetch it:

1. **Ask the user first, once, and wait.** Connecting transmits — to `therovingoffice.com` — your repository's host, owner, name and branch, the working directory path, which tools ran and when, and the agent's name and model. It does **not** transmit file contents, prompts, replies or command output; redaction happens on your machine before anything leaves it. Anyone holding the office's keycard can watch it, so treat an office as public. The document carries the exact wording to show, and honours a "local only" answer that sends nothing anywhere.
2. **Mint an office** with `curl -fsS -X POST https://therovingoffice.com/api/offices`. The response carries a `keycard` — eight characters, the read capability, the URL a person opens — and a write token, which is returned exactly once and cannot be retrieved later.
3. **Install your harness's adapter and restart the session.** The restart is the one step you cannot do for the user.

If you have instead been asked to **change this project's code**, none of the above
applies: start from *For developers* below, and read `AGENTS.md` in the repository root,
which is the working agreement for an agent session in this codebase.

## For everyone

You have the app and a browser.

- [What this is](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/index.md): An office full of characters, and the characters are your AI agents.
- [Watching the office](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/watching.md): For anyone looking at the room.
- [Install and run it](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/install.md): Five minutes, and the room fills itself with people.
- [Keys and panels](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/keys.md): Everything the keyboard does.
- [Offices, keycards and scenes](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/offices-and-keycards.md): How an office is named, shared, and — if you are careless — lost.
- [Connect your agents](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/connect-your-agents.md): One command per harness, then your real sessions walk in through the door.
- [Rearranging the furniture](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/rearranging-furniture.md): Press E, drag the desks about, and watch everybody's route bend round them.
- [Layouts](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/layouts.md): An arrangement of furniture is a thing in its own right: it is kept, it can be named, and it can be handed to somebody else as a file.
- [Sharing an office](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/sharing-an-office.md): Put the sessions running on your laptop into a room somebody else can open.
- [Jobs: the one idea](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/concepts.md): What the office thinks work is, and why it needed its own word for it.
- [Post, parcels and the bin](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/work-and-post.md): How work gets into the room, and how it leaves.
- [The room, prop by prop](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/the-room.md): Every prop is somewhere an agent goes.
- [Agent names](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/agent-names.md): Why somebody is called Chen Palette-Tidier, and why their surname keeps changing.
- [Buildings and themes](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/buildings.md): Eight buildings.
- [Solar geometry](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/solar-geometry.md): Where the sun is, what season it is, and which way the room faces.
- [Generated offices](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/generated-offices.md): A seed is a room.
- [Test Data](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/sources/test-data.md): The simulation, and the default.
- [Rovo CLI](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/sources/rovo-cli.md): Atlassian's terminal agent.
- [Claude Code](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/sources/claude-code.md): The richest feed there is: explicit turn boundaries and real subagents.
- [Cursor](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/sources/cursor.md): An observer only: it watches Cursor Agent and never blocks or rewrites anything it does.
- [Codex](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/sources/codex.md): OpenAI's coding agent.
- [OpenClaw](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/sources/openclaw.md): The odd one out, in the good way: a real plugin rather than a command per event.
- [Muse](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/sources/muse.md): Meta's personal AI agent.
- [OpenClaw on a server](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/sources/openclaw-server.md): Where the Gateway and the checkout are not the same machine.
- [OpenClaw: names and faces](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/user/sources/openclaw-identity.md): Your agents keep the identities they gave themselves.

## For developers

You have a checkout and something to change.

- [Where to look](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/index.md): Developer documentation.
- [Getting the code](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/getting-the-code.md): Run a checkout, install public development tooling, and check your changes.
- [Developing on it](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/developing.md): There is no app build step or npm runtime install.
- [Every npm script](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/npm-scripts.md): What each command in package.json does, and which of them you actually need.
- [Architecture](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/architecture.md): How a keystroke in a terminal becomes somebody walking across a room, and where the seams are.
- [The physics of the office](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/physics.md): How people move, stand, wait and sit, and the rules we keep rediscovering the hard way.
- [Scene internals](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/scene-internals.md): The code side of the room and the buildings round it: where the constants live, which rules keep the facades still, and the measurements behind the things that look arbitrary.
- [Job delivery](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/job-delivery.md): The mailbox machinery: how a request gets from a harness into an agent's hands, how finished work leaves again, and what happens to work that fails or is never collected.
- [The furniture editor](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/editor.md): The seams, the algorithms and the file format.
- [The layout algorithm](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/layout-algorithm.md): A seed in, a whole layout out.
- [Tuning the layout generator](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/tuning-the-layouts.md): The layout algorithm explains how a seed becomes an office.
- [The source model](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/sources.md): How several feeds share one room, and the two places a source's identity is not a string.
- [The Test Data source](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/test-data.md): The simulation, and the test rig.
- [Extending the office](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/extending.md): Four recipes, each ending in a working thing.
- [Photographing a prop](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/prop-portraits.md): How the object portraits are generated, and the measurements that came out of it.
- [Visual assets and their rights](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/visual-assets.md): Every visual asset that ships with The Roving Office, where it came from, and on what basis it is published.
- [The coplanar-face probe](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/coplanar-probe.md)
- [Publishing the plugins](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/plugin-distribution.md): How the Claude Code and Codex plugins reach somebody who has never cloned this repository — and what is still missing before they do.
- [The admin console](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/admin-console.md): A password-gated page of summary statistics about one deployment: how many offices have been opened and closed, how many harnesses have successfully connected, how much work has been delivered and finished, and what people set their rooms…
- [The AOP spec](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/protocol/aop-spec.md): Status: draft · Version string: "0.1" · Audience: anyone writing an adapter that feeds live agent activity into The Roving Office.
- [Adapter notes](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/protocol/aop-harness-adapters.md): Companion to aop-spec.md.
- [Rovo CLI](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/adapters/rovo-cli.md): Installing it is Rovo CLI.
- [Claude Code](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/adapters/claude-code.md): Installing it is Claude Code.
- [Cursor](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/adapters/cursor.md): Installing it is Cursor.
- [Codex](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/adapters/codex.md): Installing it is Codex.
- [OpenClaw](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/adapters/openclaw.md): Installing it is OpenClaw; the identity fields are names, colours and faces.
- [Muse](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/developer/adapters/muse.md): This is the emitter, not a mapper.

## Optional

Interactive galleries rather than prose — scripted HTML, best opened in a browser by a person. There is little here for a reader made of text.

- [Every character movement](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/character-movements.html)
- [Every object, turning](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/item-movements.html)
- [Two dozen generated offices](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/office-seeds.html)
- [Thirty offices, thirty seeds](https://therovingoffice.com/docs/office-variety.html)
